uncited: It builds on [3D Gaussian Splatting LOD methods](5439-3d-gaussian-splatting-lod-methods.md) by introducing a Split Point Tree (SPT) structure to manage the hierarchy.
H-3DGS shares the fundamental rendering equation of 3DGS, where a scene is represented as a collection of anisotropic 3D Gaussians.

Each Gaussian $G_i$ is defined by a mean position $\mu_i$, a covariance matrix $\Sigma_i$ (parameterized by a rotation matrix $R_i$ and a scaling vector $s_i$), and view-dependent color coefficients represented by spherical harmonics (SH).
The color $C$ at a pixel is computed via alpha compositing of the splatted Gaussians sorted by depth.
The core innovation of H-3DGS is the **Hierarchical Split Point Tree (HSPT)**.
This structure organizes the scene into a hierarchy of spatial partitions (chunks) and levels of detail.
During training, the scene is divided into chunks.
Each chunk is trained independently to manage memory constraints.
After training, the chunks are merged into a global hierarchy.
Prior methods for large-scale environments, such as those by Tancik et al. [2022] and Xu et al. [2023], employed scene partitioning or multi-GPU strategies.
It is used for ultra-large scale reconstruction, including aerial and street-level datasets.
